spans.text: Vroom-vroom-vroom—
As the roar of the bike engine slowly fades away, you and Saki dismount. She takes off the helmet you insisted she wear and swishes her ponytail.
Why did you ask me out so late at night. Our concert's tomorrow, you know.
Course I do, so cut the crap and follow me.
I've done that, haven't I... Atchoo!
By the way, this place is freezing.
Saki has brought you to an overlook. You gaze into the distance and see dense forest and faraway buildings.
Where is this place?
I got a question, Commander.
After riding with me so many times, what do you think of my biking skills?
...Did you eat something bad?
Are you actually asking me my opinion?
Just answer the question, dumbass! Or do you need a beating first?
Er, you're a great rider, of course.
I had a lot of bikers back in my old workplace...
But you're easily among the best of them... Anyway, since you're asking, I've got a question of my own.
Is it me or are you really bad at braking?
Tsk.
Saki plants her hands on her waist and stares into the distance before clicking her tongue in annoyance.
I can't believe even an amateur like you noticed... I guess old habits die hard?
What?
It's nothin'. I got another question, Commander.
What big things have you done in your life?
Isn't this change of topics a little extreme?
Shaddup. What have you achieved?
...Well, if you must know...
I guess I've done a few things in my time. There are some things that seem really out of this world when I think about them...
Huh... So you really DID do stuff like that before?
How does it measure up to what we're facing now?
And let me get this out of the way first, if you say our concert is just small potatoes, I'm REALLY going to let you have it.
What's the point of answering when you've ruled out all my responses...
You smile helplessly and then place both hands on the railing, letting the cold wind wash over you as you look down over the landscape.
I mean, what's there to compare?
I've lived through a lot of battlefields with my friends by my side.
Those memories aren't going to fade just because I spent time with you.
On the contrary, even if I felt nostalgic about them, I wouldn't disregard the present just because I felt that way.
If I thought your show was really small potatoes, I wouldn't have gone this far to accommodate you.
How about this, right now I'm having a stomachache... Because I know we can't afford to mess up for tomorrow's show.
Damn, you're smooth. Are you an intellectual or something? Been to school maybe?
Why? Haven't you?
Well, I did go to school, but I didn't learn anything there compared to the outside.
Plus, there were pains in the ass everywhere, so I just couldn't stay on.
Saki waves the question off and looks at you.
Allow me to teach you something you won't learn in school.
You just said I was bad at braking, right?
I do that on purpose. No matter when or where, I never think about slowing down.
...Uh, that's no good, right? I'm pretty sure that's dangerous riding.
Well, when it comes to me—I've always survived by having guts, past or present.
Saki looks down from the overlook as she said this. There are complex emotions in her eyes.
If you don't keep dashing down the straights, the no. 1 place is only going to get further and further from you.
I won't become soft and weak, not even if I die—That's how I became the boss.
You mull over what Saki's not saying and fall silent.
...I think I get the idea.
If you're thinking about braking from the get-go, your mindset goes from valuing speed to safety.
While that might be the right answer for most people, it's just a drawback for you, isn't it?
Indeed! I knew I like you for a reason, you DO understand.
Saki slaps you on the back.
Yup! That's my secret of being the boss all this time!
—That is to say, ignoring everything else and charging forward.
But... The fact that it's still dangerous hasn't changed in the least.
Maybe you've gotten by with never failing because of your luck, but it'll catch up to you someday.
...Someday, huh.
Saki doesn't get mad as you "lecture" her.
Do you know why I brought you here?
Didn't I ask you that from the very beginning?
That's because this is my deathplace—in other words, I died here.
Because this is your... Wait, what?!
You're so startled that you stumble back and almost fall down the stairs.
Your... Your...?!
What's the big fuss?
You DO know we've all died before, right?
Compared to your reaction, Saki is tremendously nonchalant about it as the decedent in question.
No... But... Er...
How did you...
Back then, we were throwing down with another crew.
While settling things with my fists isn't a problem, neither of us wanted our people to get hurt.
So we decided to settle things once and for all here.
Saki turns around and points in the direction from which you came, then turns again and points downward, on the platform you're standing on.
We decided to settle it through a game of chicken, and I went up against the boss of the other group.
We'd both ride our bikes to the edge of this overlook and the first person to brake would lose.
It is then that you realize something.
...You, you already...
Yup.
She flattens her lips and leans on the railing.
I braked too late and flew off from the side of this place.
That's what you mean by "my luck catching up to me someday", right?
I already knew that.
And you didn't learn a damn thing even after going through something like this?!
Learn a thing—? Hey! Are you kidding me, Commander?
I have never—NEVER—once regretted doing this!
Saki turns on you with a fierce look on her face.
That's right, I died. But so what?
I WON!
...So what if you won?! You lost your life too!
Of COURSE I'd like to live on if I could.
But if I ended up losing because of that, then I'd rather die! That's the most important thing to me!
Saki's spirit has completely overwhelmed yours, never mind that you believe in what is right.
Still, the guts to bet everything for the sake of victory still baffles you.
After a brief silence, you lower your head, lightly tracing the railing with your finger as you look with concern at the drop below.
...I'm sorry.
After cooling down and thinking about it, the fact that you brought me here and told me all this was because you trusted me, right?
Tsk.
The hell are you saying sorry for, I figured you'd react this way from the beginning.
Then why did you...
I didn't go out of my way to tell you all this because I wanted you to approve of me.
You thought this was about trust—you're not entirely wrong, but it's way more than just that.
No matter what others say, no matter what I have to do, I will never admit defeat.
This is the way I've lived all my life. You're my producer and also my bestie.
So no matter what... I wanted to pass this determination on to you.
..."Screw everything and charge full speed ahead, right?"
You smile bitterly and sigh.
Looks like I've got a long way to go when it comes to putting the brakes on you.
Hah?! So after hearing all that your reaction is STILL to rain on my parade?!
Then what's the point of telling you all that!
No, no, I get it. You got your point across.
But being a bestie isn't a one-way street, right? If I listen to you, then you got to listen to me, don't you think?
...Tsk.
Saki clicks her tongue, seemingly unable to respond to your words, but she doesn't say anything.
Also, you got one thing wrong..
I don't intend to stop you, BUT I'm going to make sure that your way forward leads you to the right destination. That's what a bestie ought to do.
...Ah, alright, I get it.
God, there's no arguin' with you when you say crap like that... No wait. I didn't lose. It's a draw at best.
Yep. Of course it's a draw. "Who wins" is a question that kids ask... not friends.
Heh.
Saki smiles.
I don't care about brakin' before I win.
Not when I'm racing and not when I'm performin'.
Then whether it's as Saki Nikaido or Franchouchou Member No. 2...
I'll let you be yourself as much as you want. Provided, of course, I think you're going the right way, okay?
Try it, then.
You can't help but laugh.
Well, since you've told me all this... Eh, I might as well tell you about it.
I messed up once and got captured by a bad lot.
They interrogated me for important information, and in the end I spun a lot of crap to buy time for myself.
Eh— What the hell?
I can't believe you were keeping such an interesting story from me!
Come on, fess up! Tell me all about it!
You look up to the starry sky and laugh as you have a long conversation with Saki.
It's true that she gave you a much needed shot in the arm on the eve of your greatest challenge.
—All you need to do is disregard everything and charge straight ahead.
